name: NLK
description: NLK is a Hungarian beating/shedding card game for 4-9 players in two phases. Phase One: players accumulate cards by drawing from a talon and giving away cards that fit on opponents' stacks (next rank higher). Phase Two: players try to shed their accumulated cards by beating cards in tricks. The last player holding cards loses.
deck: Variable (32-52 cards depending on player count)

history.origins: NLK is a Hungarian card game learned from students at Szeged University. The initials stand for an obscene Hungarian phrase: N=nagy (big), L=any nationality starting with L (litvÃ¡n, lengyel, luxemburgi), K=kibaszÃ³s (roughly 'screwing'). The game is light-hearted and best with about six players.
timeline: 20th Century: Game played in Hungarian universities
1997: Rules documented by Gyula Zsigri and Gábor Sperla
Present: Played in Hungary and by card game enthusiasts
history.cultural: Associated with Hungarian university culture and social gatherings. The humorous name reflects the playful, irreverent attitude of student card games.
history.evolution: The game has remained relatively stable in its rules. The two-phase structure (accumulation followed by shedding) is its distinctive feature.

setup.players: 4-9 players. Deal and play are anticlockwise.
setup.deck: Variable size: 4 players=32 cards (A-7), 5 players=36 cards (A-6), 6 players=40 cards (A-5), 9 players=52 cards (A-2). Cards rank A-K-Q-J-10-9-8-7-6-5-4-3-2.
setup.dealing: One card dealt face-up to each player. Remaining cards form the talon (face-down stack).
setup.equipment: Variable deck size based on player count.

rules.objective: Avoid being the last player holding cards at the end of Phase Two.
rules.gameplay: Two phases. Phase One: take turns anticlockwise; draw the top card of the talon and place it on your stack, and optionally give away cards from your stack or drawn talon cards onto opponents' stacks when a card fits (next rank above; lowest rank fits on Ace). Phase Two: play in tricks; beat the previous card with a higher card of the same suit or a trump, or pick up the lowest card in the trick. Last player left holding cards loses.
keyRules: Phase One: accumulate cards, give away cards that fit (next rank higher)
Phase Two: shed cards by beating; pick up lowest if can't beat
No obligation to follow suit in Phase Twoâ€”just must beat or pick up
Trumps determined by last talon card drawn

strategy.basic: In Phase One, try to accumulate a small stack by giving away cards whenever possible. Cards that fit on opponents' stacks are your friends.
strategy.intermediate: Plan your Phase Two hand during Phase One. Keep track of which cards you've seen. The trump suit is unknown until the last talon cardâ€”plan for flexibility.
strategy.advanced: In Phase Two, sometimes picking up a low card is better than using a high card to beat. Save your high cards for when you really need them. Force opponents to pick up by playing cards they can't easily beat.
tips: In Phase One, Aces are dangerous because only the lowest rank can fit on them
Watch the talon sizeâ€”when it's low, prepare for Phase Two
Picking up the lowest card in a trick can be strategic if it gives you a useful card

scoring.description: Hand-based; loser is last player with cards. Loser deals next hand.
scoring.winCondition: Avoid being last player holding cards.

synthesis.shortDescription: A Hungarian card game in two phases: first accumulate cards by giving away cards that 'fit', then shed your hand by beating cards or picking up the lowest.
